translations.en: Amr ibn Shimr, Abu Abdillah, al-Ju'fi.

chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام) وَجَابِرَ. ضَعِيفٌ.

translations.en: He narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Jabir. Weak.

en.summary: Amr ibn Shimr al-Ju'fi, a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), is recorded in al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* as a narrator who transmitted from both the Imam and Jabir ibn Yazid. Although classified as 'weak' (da'if) in terms of individual reliability, his status is significant in Shia scholarship because he is often cited as a bridge to the more reliable Jabir, highlighting the nuanced evaluation of narrators within the Ja'fari tradition. This classification underscores the importance of distinguishing between a narrator's personal integrity and their precision in transmission when verifying hadith authority.
en.seo_question: Who is Amr ibn Shimr and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.عَمْرُو بْنُ شَمْرٍ: Amr ibn Shimr, the narrator's name
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a kunya (honorific) referring to Imam al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْجَعْفِيُّ: Al-Ju'fi, a nisba indicating lineage or association with the Banu Ju'fa tribe
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator is not fully reliable
